comparison_scope: Functional contract comparison of exact validation-command grouping against the existing actions target coverage, Actions interval, execution Pareto, and per-run attribution tools. The input unit, matching key, and output are distinct. No same-task performance, reliability, cost, or operator-time benchmark was conducted.
findings: The new planner groups exact caller-declared argv and execution-context signatures across validation profiles and refuses to call a group reusable unless each member declares source-reviewed read-only behavior.
The target-coverage comparator compares selected validation targets and declared outcomes across multiple runs; it does not group command invocations across component profiles.
The interval-union tool summarizes elapsed job intervals; it does not establish invocation identity or decide reuse.
The execution Pareto tool compares caller-declared outcomes and one resource metric across candidates; it does not analyze profile command signatures.
The single-run attribution tool binds one plan, run, artifact set, and optional receipt; it does not group validators across multiple profiles.
All four incumbent tools retain their stated task scopes. No incumbent is retired or replaced.
unknowns: Whether a future executor can safely fan one real process result out to every grouped profile without losing profile-specific assertions.
Any latency, billing, operator-time, reliability, or generalizable process-saving effect.
claim_ceiling: A bounded functional scope comparison supports specialized coexistence. It does not establish a performance win, production CI safety, or coverage of all valuable incumbent uses.
